records.claim_text: A commitment identifies costs that will be incurred in the future for materials or services already requested or ordered.
records.evidence_quote: Identifies costs that will be incurred in the future for materials and services that you have requested or ordered.

records.claim_text: Commitments reserve funds for costs that will be incurred at a future date.
records.evidence_quote: Commitments reserve funds for costs that will be incurred at a future date.

records.claim_text: SAP distinguishes three commitment types by account assignment object: order commitment, cost center commitment, and project commitment.
records.evidence_quote: Commitments Management distinguishes between three types of commitments, depending on the account assignment object:

records.claim_text: A project commitment is initially assigned to a project or to a work breakdown structure element.
records.evidence_quote: The commitment is initially assigned to a project, or to a work breakdown structure element.

records.claim_text: Purchase requisitions express an internal requirement and are freely changeable; purchase orders are contractual and cannot be changed unilaterally.
records.evidence_quote: Purchase orders are contractual requests to a vendor, to supply certain goods or services according to the agreed conditions.

records.claim_text: Funds commitments reserve funds for costs that are fairly certain but not yet tied to a requisition or order.
records.evidence_quote: You can use Funds Commitments to reserve funds for costs you are fairly certain to incur

records.claim_text: Purchase requisition commitment equals the remaining requisition quantity multiplied by the requisition price.
records.evidence_quote: The system calculates purchase requisition commitments from the remaining quantity of a purchase requisition, which it multiplies with the price

records.claim_text: PR commitments are reduced on a quantity basis by purchase orders that reference the corresponding purchase requisition.
records.evidence_quote: The system reduces PReq commitments on a quantity basis, using purchase orders referring to the corresponding purchase requisition.

records.claim_text: A PR commitment goes to zero either via a purchase order for the full amount or via a change to the requisition.
records.evidence_quote: The system reduces a PReq commitment to zero using a purchase order with the full amount, or using a change in the purchase requisition.

records.claim_text: Worked example: a requisition of 5 pieces at EUR 1500.00 creates a purchase requisition commitment of EUR 7500.00.
records.evidence_quote: You create a purchase requisition for 5 PCs at EUR 1500.00. This leads to a purchase requisition commitment of EUR 7500.00.

records.claim_text: Ordering only part of a requisition reduces the PR commitment proportionally at the requisition price, not the PO price.
records.evidence_quote: The system reduces the purchase requisition commitment in proportion to quantity to EUR 3,000.00 (3 x EUR 1,500.00 = EUR 4,500.00).

records.claim_text: The purchase requisition commitment forms part of availability control against the project budget.
records.evidence_quote: The resulting purchase requisition commitment also forms part of the availability control.

records.claim_text: Purchase order commitments reduce the referenced purchase requisition commitment; PO commitments are then reduced by goods/invoice receipt logic.
records.evidence_quote: Purchase order commitments reduce each purchase requisition commitment by referencing to a purchase requisition.

records.claim_text: Purchase order commitments are reduced according to the goods receipt / invoice receipt logic.
records.evidence_quote: Purchase order commitments are reduced according to the goods / invoice receipt logic .

records.claim_text: Commitments Management must be explicitly activated before commitment values are recorded.
records.evidence_quote: You must activate Commitments Management before you can use it.

records.claim_text: The purchase order commitment is the order value for which no actual costs have yet been incurred.
records.evidence_quote: It is the value of goods ordered, but for which no actual costs have yet been incurred.

records.claim_text: A purchase order only produces a commitment if it is account-assigned to an order, cost center, or project.
records.evidence_quote: For this data transfer to take place from Purchasing, the purchase order must be assigned to an order, a cost center, or a project.

records.claim_text: Commitments are dated by the expected delivery date, not the purchase order creation date.
records.evidence_quote: You create commitments using the expected delivery date, not the date the purchase order was created.

records.claim_text: The purchase order commitment includes anticipated delivery costs, managed separately from the order value itself.
records.evidence_quote: A purchase order commitment includes anticipated delivery costs. These costs are managed separately by the system.

records.claim_text: Delivery costs within a commitment are displayed individually by origin such as freight, duty, and packaging.
records.evidence_quote: They are displayed individually according to origin (for example, freight costs, duty costs, packaging).

records.claim_text: A purchase order item can be split across several account assignment objects; the commitment is updated on each accordingly.
records.evidence_quote: The system updates the purchase order commitment on the corresponding account assignment objects accordingly.

records.claim_text: Re-assigning a purchase order item to a different cost object is allowed only while no actual costs have been incurred.
records.evidence_quote: You can only do this if no actual costs have yet been incurred. Therefore, no goods receipt or invoice receipt may already have occurred.

records.claim_text: The system reduces purchase order commitments to zero according to goods or invoice receipts and converts them into actual costs.
records.evidence_quote: The system reduces purchase order commitments to zero according to goods or invoice receipts and converts them into actual costs.

records.claim_text: The goods receipt indicator on the purchase order item decides whether commitment reduction and actual cost arise at GR or at IR.
records.evidence_quote: The goods receipt indicator in the purchase order determines when the commitment is reduced and actual costs are set up

records.claim_text: With the GR indicator set on the purchase order item, the commitment is reduced when goods are received.
records.evidence_quote: GR indicator set: Commitment is reduced when goods are received.

records.claim_text: Reduction to zero is quantity-driven, so quantity-based commitment management is required; value-based management is an alternative configuration.
records.evidence_quote: As the quantity (down to zero) determines the reduction of a purchase order commitment to zero, you need quantity-based commitment management.

records.claim_text: Purchase orders for services are monitored on the basis of value, not quantity, unlike material purchase orders.
records.evidence_quote: Unlike purchase orders for materials, those for services are monitored on the basis of value, not quantity.

records.claim_text: Entering a goods receipt or invoice receipt against a purchase order reduces the commitment proportionally.
records.evidence_quote: You can reduce the purchase order commitment proportionally . To do this, you need to enter a goods receipt or invoice receipt

records.claim_text: When the ordered quantity is under-delivered and no further delivery is expected, the Delivery completed indicator must be set at goods receipt.
records.evidence_quote: In this case, you must set the "Delivery completed" indicator when you post the goods receipt.

records.claim_text: At invoice entry a final-invoice indicator can be set on the purchase order item to signal no further invoices are expected.
records.evidence_quote: you can set the indicator in the purchase order item to indicate that you do not expect any more incoming invoices

records.claim_text: Locking a purchase order item to prevent goods receipt is a documented way to reduce its commitment completely.
records.evidence_quote: If you lock a purchase order item to prevent goods receipt for that item.

records.claim_text: Only completed purchase order items can be deleted; outstanding items require the Delivery completed indicator first.
records.evidence_quote: If you wish to delete outstanding items, you need to set the "Delivery completed" indicator in the purchase order item first.

records.claim_text: In SAP's worked example an invoice priced above the PO raises both actual and assigned totals from 4650.00 to 6150.00.
records.evidence_quote: 3. Invoice receipt for three PCs, USD 2,000.00 each

records.claim_text: The final goods receipt reduces the purchase order commitment fully and converts it into actual costs.
records.evidence_quote: You post the last goods receipt using a PC. The purchase order commitment is reduced and converted completely into actual costs.

records.claim_text: SAP commitment reports present three columns: Actual, Commitments, and Assigned defined as actual plus commitment.
records.evidence_quote: Assigned (actual + commitment)

records.claim_text: Freight added to a purchase order is included in the commitment: 3 pieces at 1500.00 plus 150.00 freight commits 4650.00.
records.evidence_quote: 1. Purchase Order Three Pcs à USD 1500.00 + USD 150.00 Freight

records.claim_text: PO commitment reduction is driven by follow-on documents posted against the purchasing document, including goods receipt, invoice and credit memo.
records.evidence_quote: the commitment reduction, and as consequence, the consumption confirmation, is processed based on the related documents posted against the purchasing document

records.claim_text: The goods-receipt-non-valuated flag controls whether the commitment decreases at goods receipt or only when an invoice is posted.
records.evidence_quote: controls whether the commitment is decreased when goods are received or when an invoice has been posted

records.claim_text: For quantity-based commitment items the reduction uses the goods receipt or invoice quantity, not its value.
records.evidence_quote: For positions that are using quantity-based commitments, the commitments will be reduced based on the quantity from the goods receipt/invoice and not in the value.

records.claim_text: For non-service items purchase requisition commitment reduction is always quantity-based; value-based reduction applies only to service items.
records.evidence_quote: For non-service items, the purchasing requisitions commitments reductions is always quantity based (note 355793).

records.claim_text: Goods receipt cancellations and credit memos reverse consumption, reducing the recorded receipt values and quantities and restoring commitment.
records.evidence_quote: Documents, that reduces the consumption, as goods receipt canceling or credit memo are used to reduce the values and quantities

records.claim_text: Delivery costs are incorporated into the item effective price and are therefore also committed, then reduced by GR and invoice documents.
records.evidence_quote: The reductions of the committed delivery cost are also processed for debit documents as GR and IV.

records.claim_text: Setting the final delivery flag ELIKZ on the order item drives the commitment completely to zero on the delivery route.
records.evidence_quote: the flag 'final delivery' (ELIKZ) is set in the order item, then the commitment will be completely reduced (set to zero)

records.claim_text: The same total-reduction behaviour applies on the invoice route when the final invoice flag EREKZ is set.
records.evidence_quote: The same applies with commitment reduction via invoice with the flag 'final invoice' set (EREKZ).

records.claim_text: Deleting a purchase order item also deletes the corresponding commitments.
records.evidence_quote: When a position has been deleted (LOEKZ), the corresponding commitments are also deleted.

records.claim_text: Commitment line items store both original and open figures; open value equals purchased value minus reduced value.
records.evidence_quote: WHGBTR - open value in local currency (purchased value – reduced value)

records.claim_text: With multiple account assignment, partial invoice amounts are distributed either progressively (fill-up) or proportionally per the partial invoice indicator.
records.evidence_quote: If you enter a partial invoice at invoice receipt, the system calculates the distribution of the costs in invoice verification

records.claim_text: Purchase order account assignment can only be changed while no goods receipt or invoice has been posted.
records.evidence_quote: The account information on the purchasing order can only be changed if no goods receipt or invoices have been posted.

records.claim_text: Invoices may carry account assignments not present on the purchase order; these unplanned values are distributed across the planned accounts.
records.evidence_quote: Values from unplanned accounts are distributed among the planned accounts in “Follow in a row” way.

records.claim_text: SAP provides a repair report that rebuilds commitment data from the purchase order and its document history.
records.evidence_quote: This report rebuilds the commitment information based on the purchasing order information and purchasing order history.

records.claim_text: Commitments for stock transport orders are switched on via a dedicated enhancement, i.e. they are not on by default.
records.evidence_quote: ME_COMM_STO_ACTIVE_CHECK – commitments for stock transport orders.

records.claim_text: A network-generated purchase requisition creates a PR commitment on the activity or WBS element account assignment object.
records.evidence_quote: The purchase requisition results in purchase requisition commitments for the account assignment object (activity or WBS element).

records.claim_text: Converting the requisition to a purchase order produces a purchase order commitment carrying a different value type from the PR commitment.
records.evidence_quote: When you convert the purchase requisition to a purchase order, it results in purchase order commitments for the account assignment object

records.claim_text: Whether actual costs post at goods receipt or invoice receipt depends on the account assignment category (valuated vs non-valuated GR).
records.evidence_quote: Based on the account assignment category of the purchase order, actual costs are posted upon goods receipt or invoice receipt

records.claim_text: Account assignment category F is the standard for order account assignment and produces a valuated goods receipt.
records.evidence_quote: For account assignment category F, the good receipt is valuated.

records.claim_text: Goods receipt for services is a two-step act: entering the services performed and then accepting them.
records.evidence_quote: Goods receipt for services involves two steps: entering the services performed and accepting the services.

records.claim_text: A service activity can hold a hierarchy of planned services plus value limits covering unplanned services.
records.evidence_quote: it can also contain a hierarchy of planned services to be purchased and value limits for unplanned services

records.claim_text: Differences between the preliminary goods receipt value at net PO price and the invoice value post to the account assignment object.
records.evidence_quote: You post any differences between the preliminary goods receipt value (net purchase order price) and invoice value to the account assignment object.

records.claim_text: Non-stock component goods receipts post as expense to the activity, not to inventory accounts, at net purchase order price.
records.evidence_quote: You post the goods receipt for the non-stock component as an expense, and not to inventory accounts.

records.claim_text: A price variance arising during invoice processing is posted to the activity that carried the goods receipt.
records.evidence_quote: If a price variance occurs during invoice processing, the variance is posted to the activity.

records.claim_text: When commitment accounting is active for the controlling area, open purchase order items on a project are recorded as commitments.
records.evidence_quote: If commitment accounting for the controlling area is active, the open purchase order items for the project are recorded as commitments.

records.claim_text: The goods receipt reduces the project commitment by the amount of the purchase order value for the received quantity.
records.evidence_quote: The goods receipt reduces the commitment by the amount of the purchase order value.

records.claim_text: Value type 11 records a posting as a statistical actual value, used for reporting project stock without real cost effect.
records.evidence_quote: You use value type 11 to record a posting as a statistical actual value.

records.claim_text: In S/4HANA the new commitment management stores commitments as forecast expenses in ACDOCA within an extension ledger.
records.evidence_quote: In S/4HANA, commitments are forecast expenses that are saved in ACDOCA in the extension ledger.

records.claim_text: Posting the actual goods receipt reverses the forecast purchasing cost in the commitment extension ledger, preventing double counting.
records.evidence_quote: When the actual goods receipt for the purchase order is posted, the forecast material purchasing costs are reversed in the enhancement ledger.

records.claim_text: The new S/4HANA commitment management supports only WBS elements and cost centers as account assignment types.
records.evidence_quote: Only projects (WBS elements) and cost centers are supported as account assignment types.

records.claim_text: An order commitment arises in the amount of the order value and incoming goods reduce it.
records.evidence_quote: An order commitment arises in the amount of the order value.

records.claim_text: Only valuated goods receipts consume budget and reduce the purchase order commitment.
records.evidence_quote: Only valuated goods receipts consume budgets and reduce the commitment from the purchase orders.

records.claim_text: If the goods receipt was non-valuated or no delivery was expected, the supplier invoice is what reduces the commitment.
records.evidence_quote: If the goods receipt was non-valuated or no delivery was expected, the supplier invoice reduces the commitment

records.claim_text: After a valuated goods receipt the later invoice only moves the number if price or quantity changes are posted during invoice processing.
records.evidence_quote: If the goods receipt was valuated, budget is only influenced if price/quantity changes are posted during invoice processing.

records.claim_text: Down payments reduce the purchase order separately, using their own budget consumption amount type.
records.evidence_quote: Down payments reduce the purchase orders separately (using a specific budget consumption amount type).

records.claim_text: Purchase requisitions and their budget consumption are reduced by the purchase orders raised against them.
records.evidence_quote: Purchase requisitions and the correspondent budget consumptions are reduced by purchase orders.

records.claim_text: Unplanned delivery costs are not agreed in the purchase order and first appear when the invoice is received.
records.evidence_quote: Unplanned delivery costs were not agreed on in the purchase order and are not entered until the invoice is received.

records.claim_text: Unplanned delivery costs are distributed automatically in the ratio of value invoiced so far to values in the current invoice.
records.evidence_quote: The system distributes the unplanned delivery costs automatically in the ratio of the value invoiced so far to the values in the current invoice.

records.claim_text: Posting unplanned delivery costs to a separate G/L account means they do not debit stock accounts or account assignment objects.
records.evidence_quote: The system posts unplanned delivery costs to a separate G/L account. Therefore, the unplanned delivery costs do not debit stock accounts or account assignment objects.

records.claim_text: Unplanned distributed delivery costs cannot be distinguished from price variances in the purchase order history.
records.evidence_quote: You cannot differentiate between unplanned distributed delivery costs and price variances in the purchase order history.

records.claim_text: If the related goods items are already settled, unplanned delivery costs are entered as a subsequent debit on the settled invoice items.
records.evidence_quote: you enter data for the unplanned delivery costs as a Subsequent Debit for the settled invoice items

records.claim_text: Retention is the part of an invoice amount held back until a defined due date such as the end of a warranty period.
records.evidence_quote: Part of an invoice amount that is retained until a defined due date (for example, the end of the warranty period)

records.claim_text: Retention is defined on the purchase order as a percentage of purchase order value at header or item level and defaults into invoice verification.
records.evidence_quote: In the purchase order, you define a retention as a percentage of the purchase order value at header or item level.

records.claim_text: Planned delivery costs are excluded from the retention calculation base.
records.evidence_quote: Plannend delivery costs are not included when retentions are calculated.

records.claim_text: Retention posts to financial accounting under a special G/L indicator, by default H.
records.evidence_quote: The system transfers the special G/L indicator for retention (by default H, can also be defined manually) to financial accounting.

records.claim_text: Retention cannot be combined with prepayment of an invoice.
records.evidence_quote: You cannot use retention together with prepayment of an invoice.

records.claim_text: Down payments on investment measures are acquisition postings normally flagged by a separate cost element.
records.evidence_quote: Down payments made for investment measures represent acquisition postings that are generally indicated by a separate cost element.

records.claim_text: Down payments can be assigned directly to an order or project, or to purchase orders that are themselves assigned to a project.
records.evidence_quote: In addition to direct account assignment to an order or project, it is also possible to assign down payments to purchase orders.

records.claim_text: Down payments show only temporarily as costs on the project, posted through a primary cost element and cleared at settlement.
records.evidence_quote: Posting as a primary cost element is necessary for the temporary display of down payments as costs in project/order cost accounting.

records.claim_text: Down payment and its clearing must be settled together under the same settlement rule so they net to zero.
records.evidence_quote: you must ensure that the down payment and down payment clearing are settled together with the same settlement rule

records.claim_text: Down payments cannot be transferred from a network to a WBS element and must be assigned directly to the WBS element.
records.evidence_quote: Down payments cannot be transferred from a network to a WBS element.

records.claim_text: Services actually performed are recorded on service entry sheets referencing the purchase order.
records.evidence_quote: You enter services that have actually been performed by means of service entry sheets.

records.claim_text: Unplanned services entered against a purchase order value limit are recorded at precise value and checked against that limit.
records.evidence_quote: The services are recorded with their precise value, and the system checks that the limit has not been exceeded.

records.claim_text: Service acceptance can be separated from service entry to preserve the dual control principle.
records.evidence_quote: You can separate the process of service acceptance from that of service entry in order to maintain the dual control principle.

records.claim_text: A service entry sheet under a multi-level release procedure counts as accepted only after the last release point approves.
records.evidence_quote: The document is not regarded as accepted until the last release point has released it.

records.claim_text: Service invoice verification compares the accepted entry sheet value with the invoice value and warns if the entry sheet value is exceeded.
records.evidence_quote: If the value in the entry sheet is exceeded, the system issues a warning message.

records.claim_text: Cumulative actual values for services performed are continually updated in the underlying purchase order during performance.
records.evidence_quote: the cumulative " actual" values (for the services actually performed) are continually updated in the underlying purchase order

records.claim_text: All movements of materials held as project stock pass through project stock using MM movement types with special stock indicator Q.
records.evidence_quote: You post such movements using MM movement types, with special stock indicator Q.

records.claim_text: A material component entered with negative quantity represents an issue of material from the network activity back into project stock.
records.evidence_quote: Material components with a negative quantity represent issues of material from the network activity to stock.

records.claim_text: For project stock items the standard account assignment category is Q and the stock-bearing WBS element is the account assignment element.
records.evidence_quote: In the standard system, account assignment category Q is used for items in purchasing documents

records.claim_text: In valuated project stock, procurement actual costs land on the WBS element and usage actual costs land on the activity.
records.evidence_quote: actual costs from material procurement are recorded in the WBS element and those from materials usage are recorded in the activity

records.claim_text: Internal activity allocation is one of the enumerated sources from which network actual costs arise.
records.evidence_quote: Network actual costs arise from:

records.claim_text: Plan values of appended networks raise WBS plan values, while apportioned network values raise the WBS assigned value.
records.evidence_quote: Plan values in appended networks increase the plan values in the relevant WBS element: apportioned values increase the assigned value.

records.claim_text: Internal activity allocation and assigned CO orders are among the business transactions that post actual data to the project.
records.evidence_quote: Internal activity allocation, assigned CO orders (CO)

records.claim_text: Goods issue for reservations in inventory management is a documented source of project actual data.
records.evidence_quote: Inventory Management: goods issue for reservations (MM)

records.claim_text: Costs incurred are posted directly to the WBS element, the network, or the activity according to account assignment.
records.evidence_quote: Costs incurred are posted directly to the WBS, network, or activity.

records.claim_text: Actual costs posted on orders attached to a project count as assigned funds for the WBS elements until settlement.
records.evidence_quote: Although actual costs are posted to orders, they are representing assigned funds for the WBS elements.

records.claim_text: A project or its work packages must be released before actual data can be entered against it.
records.evidence_quote: You must release the project (or the work packages) before you can enter actual data.

records.claim_text: Estimate at completion equals actual plus commitment costs already incurred plus the updated cost to complete.
records.evidence_quote: The resulting figure is arrived at by adding the actual and commitment costs already incurred in the project to the updated cost to complete.

records.claim_text: Commitment values from periods before the forecast key date are recorded in the forecast version at the key date period.
records.evidence_quote: Commitment values from periods before the period of the cost forecast key date are recorded in the forecast version

records.claim_text: Overhead on actual and commitment values must be calculated separately before estimating costs at completion.
records.evidence_quote: You must calculate the overhead on actual and commitment values separately for the calculation of the estimated costs at completion.

records.claim_text: Marking an activity complete or issuing a final confirmation sets its cost to complete to zero.
records.evidence_quote: If an activity is marked as complete or there is a final confirmation for it, the system sets the cost to complete to zero.

records.claim_text: Commitment carry-forward moves a commitment into the first period of the following fiscal year via a dedicated transaction.
records.evidence_quote: To carry forward a commitment to the first period of the following fiscal year, proceed as follows:

records.claim_text: Commitment carry-forward supports a test run that computes without updating, and a reversal indicator to undo a prior carry-forward.
records.evidence_quote: The Reversal indicator controls whether data that has already been carried forward is reversed again.

records.claim_text: Commitment carry-forward moves commitments from the last period of a fiscal year to the first period of the next year.
records.evidence_quote: You use the commitment carryforward function to carry commitments for a sales order forward from the last period of a fiscal year

records.claim_text: A commitment plan pre-plans value consumption on purchase contracts, generating a plan for each contract document item.
records.evidence_quote: You can use the commitment plan to preplan value consumption on purchase contracts.

records.claim_text: Each commitment plan item generates an earmarked funds document that is copied onto referencing purchase requisitions and orders.
records.evidence_quote: If a purchase requisition or purchase order references this contract, the earmarked funds document is copied to the purchase order

records.claim_text: Once the earmarked funds document is copied from the contract, assigning to a different account assignment object is disallowed.
records.evidence_quote: Account assignment to a different account assignment object is then no longer allowed.

records.claim_text: For projects, availability control can check against either the current budget or the released budget.
records.evidence_quote: For projects, availability control can check against the current budget or the released budget.

records.claim_text: Current budget is the original budget together with budget supplements, budget returns, and budget transfers.
records.evidence_quote: The _Current budget_ column displays the original budget together with the budget supplements, budget returns, and budget transfers.

records.claim_text: Commitment management must be active for the controlling area and current fiscal year before commitments are recorded.
records.evidence_quote: First, in the Controlling Area, Commitment Management must be active for the current fiscal year (transaction OKKP).

records.claim_text: Account assignment cannot be changed on goods receipt documents, unlike on invoices where unplanned accounts are permitted.
records.evidence_quote: On goods receipt documents it’s not possible to change the account information.

records.claim_text: A dedicated routine checks on every purchase order change whether anything commitment-relevant has changed before re-sending to accounting.
records.evidence_quote: It also check when a PO has been changed if something relevant for the commitments has been changed.

records.claim_text: The PO communication structure must always carry both purchase order and receipt/invoice quantities and values, regardless of the triggering event.
records.evidence_quote: the purchasing quantities and values and the goods receipt quantities and values are also relevant and should be correctly available

records.claim_text: When the GR indicator is not set on the purchase order item, the commitment is reduced when invoices are received.
records.evidence_quote: GR Indicator is not set: Commitment is reduced when invoices are received.

records.claim_text: The Assigned column on a project budget view only appears when availability control is active for the project.
records.evidence_quote: The _Assigned_ column only displays if the availability control is active for the project.

records.claim_text: If budget releases are used, availability control must run against the released budget rather than the current budget.
records.evidence_quote: If you work with budget releases, you need to also perform availability control against the released budget and not against the current budget.
